threads.body: The recursion removes optional fields from dataclasses inside `Any` payloads: a nested `Result(detail=None)` with `detail: str | None` becomes `{}` instead of `{"detail": null}`. It also runs `get_type_hints()` on user payloads, which can raise `NameError` for annotations unavailable at runtime. Preserve the previous non-filtering `asdict` conversion throughout `Any` subtrees (`arguments`, `response`, and `parameters`), with regression tests for nested dataclasses.

The `Any` fields have no default, which means instrumentations must populate them even if they want to omit the value..

Maybe you can scan the repo and see how instrumentations are passing `None` for these Any values -- are they legit `None` values, or does the instrumentation use this when they are missing..

If `None` is a legit value in some cases, we should maybe use a sentinel default value to differentiate between None and missing.. There's some discussion on the best way to do this: https://stackoverflow.com/questions/69239403/type-hinting-parameters-with-a-sentinel-value-as-the-default ..

replies.body: Looking at the 5 `Any` fields in `types.py`, `FunctionToolDefinition.parameters`, `ServerToolCallPart.server_tool_call`, and `ServerToolCallResponsePart.server_tool_call_response` are typed object schemas in semconv (not `Any` payloads), and instrumentations pass `None` for both `FunctionToolDefinition.parameters` and `ToolCallRequestPart.arguments` when unset. Since existing callers already pass `None` explicitly (and `ToolCallRequestPart.arguments` precedes non-default fields), maybe we should omit `None` on everything except `ToolCallResponsePart.response` rather than keying off `is not Any` or adding a sentinel?

@DylanRussell Anthropic sets `arguments=None` for a tool input that is not a dict. Google GenAI sets `parameters=None` for plain callables.

Nothing passes None for `server_tool_call` or `server_tool_call_response`.

`response` is None when a tool result has no content, as in bedrock and anthropic.

e092a5e drops None for every other field. `_unset_when_none` is gone with it, which also settles the `DataclassInstance` suggestion.
